court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Govind Shankar Malme vs Bhagwan Govind Malme (Deceased)

parties.respondent_defendant: Bhagwan Govind Malme (Deceased) Through LRs - Chingubai Bhagwan Malme & Ors.

facts_of_case: Partition suit filed by Bhagwan against Govind. Trial court decreed four shares in the suit property. Appellants are illegitimate sons of Govind. Appeal is against modification of decree by lower appellate court.

legal_principles.principle: Illegitimate children do not have a share in ancestral joint family properties during the lifetime of their parents.
legal_principles.held: The appeal court held that original defendant nos. 2 and 3, who are admittedly illegitimate sons of Govind, did not have any right in the suit property during the lifetime of Govind.
cited_cases: Revanasiddappa vs. Mallikarjun, (2011) 11 Supreme Court Cases 1

legal_principles.principle: Children of void or voidable marriages are entitled to a share in ancestral or joint family property only after the death of their parents.
legal_principles.held: The court held that they had a share in such property, whether the property be self-acquired or joint family property of their parents, upon its partition in favour of their parents; they may even seek partition of joint family property based on the share claimed by them from their parents but that could only be after their parents' death;
cited_cases: Revanasiddappa vs. Mallikarjun, (2011) 11 Supreme Court Cases 1
keywords: children of void or voidable marriages

outcome.final_order: Original decree modified to determine two shares in favour of Govind and Bhagwan, and no share for original defendant nos. 2 and 3.

use_for_drafting: drafting a second appeal in a partition suit
advising on the rights of illegitimate children
guidance on the application of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
